package_info.package_versions: All versions after attacker takes over the abandoned username and publishes a new version
package_info.why_malicious: The package is considered malicious because an attacker can take over an abandoned GitHub username and publish a new package with the same repository name, poisoning the supply chain. This allows the attacker to inject arbitrary malicious code into any downstream project or tool that depends on the original package, leading to widespread compromise.

execution_context.file_location: any .go source file in the malicious package (e.g., logrus.go)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code enumerates running processes, exfiltrates the process list to a remote C2 server via HTTP GET, receives and executes remote commands, and drops/executes an embedded payload, enabling remote code execution and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs process enumeration, data exfiltration to an external domain, remote command execution, and payload dropping, all of which are classic malware behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate Go package, especially a logging library, should not enumerate processes, communicate with external C2 servers, or execute arbitrary commands/payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Process enumeration and remote command execution may be used in legitimate remote management tools, but never in a general-purpose library or as an undocumented side effect.
key_indicators: remote command execution based on C2 response
use of process enumeration in a non-management library

attack_chain.action: Attacker claims abandoned GitHub username and publishes a malicious package with the same repository name.
attack_chain.leads_to: Developers and CI/CD systems fetch the malicious package.

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is imported by downstream projects (directly or as a dependency).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes at import-time on developer or production systems.

attack_chain.action: Malicious init function executes: collects process list, exfiltrates data, receives and executes remote commands, and drops/executes payloads.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote attacker gains code execution and data exfiltration capabilities on victim systems.

behavioral_signatures: Go package init functions performing network requests
HTTP requests to untrusted or hardcoded domains during import-time
Remote command execution triggered by C2 server response
Payload dropper logic embedded in library code
file_indicators: Unexpected init() functions in Go library code
References to external domains (e.g., badguy.com) in Go source
Use of ps.Processes(), exec.Command, ioutil.TempFile in non-management libraries
network_indicators: HTTP GET requests to suspicious domains (e.g., badguy.com)
Outbound connections during go build, test, or import
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Go packages that contain init functions with side effects, especially those making network requests or executing commands. Scan dependencies for references to suspicious domains or process enumeration APIs. Use static analysis to flag unexpected use of exec.Command, ps.Processes, or embedded payloads in libraries. Monitor build and runtime environments for unexpected outbound network activity during dependency resolution or import.
